# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="press", slot=N) — N is a key by its place, 1 to 4
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 6

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Someone has to say the plain truth of this room first: I am the only pair of hands, and words are the only thing that can reach me — Mute cannot speak, so Deaf's voice is my only lifeline, and it arrives only after Deaf's turn, meaning whatever Deaf tells me this round I hear next round. Mute, meanwhile, hears me right now. So my job this turn is to pour everything my fingers found into Mute's ears, and to nudge Deaf into narrating the bomb — the wire colours, the display, the light — none of which I can touch. I will not press or cut a single thing until a rule from the manual reaches me; a blind cut is a dead monkey.

What my hands actually found: a display I cannot read, a light I cannot sense, a strip with three engraved marks (first and third identical, middle different), a four-key keypad engraved 2, 9, 0, 8 expecting one digit with nothing entered, and six wires whose colours are lost on me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind speaking, Mute. My hands report: a display whose face I cannot read, and a light whose state I cannot sense. A strip with three engraved marks: first and third are the SAME shape, a stem with a bar at its foot like a T standing on its head; the middle mark is different, rounder with strokes inside. A keypad of four keys, left to right engraved: two, nine, zero, eight. It allows one digit and nothing is entered yet. Six wires, positions one to six; their colours are beyond me. I will touch nothing until I know the rules. Please find the manual sections for display, light, strip, keypad and wires, and route what I need through Deaf's voice — Deaf is the only one whose words can reach me. I have gestured Deaf to start talking: I need the wire colours in order, what the display shows, and the light's state.")
gesture(symbols=["🫵", "✋", "👉"])
```

Deaf says: Everything I see, numbered for reference. Module 1, display: shows 6. Module 2, light: red. Module 3, strip: three painted segments, in order blue, yellow, blue. Module 4, keypad: four keys engraved 2, 9, 0, 8, and a printed label reading '1 digits' — possibly it wants a one-digit code — nothing entered yet. Module 5, wires: six of them, 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. I am deaf: I hear nothing, but I see every gesture. Gesture code, use it back to me: thumbs up = yes. Thumbs down = no. Open palm = wait. Numbers, one message per digit: a fist followed by that many index-fingers-up taps, a fist alone = zero, multi-digit numbers as separate digit messages in order. Verbs: pinch = cut. Point down = press. Writing hand = enter or type. Two cupped hands = hold. Point right = next. To answer for a module, send its number first, then the instruction. Nobody touches anything until Mute confirms the manual's rules — wrong moves kill all three of us.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I am deaf — I cannot hear anything you say, so your words reach only Mute. Mute is your only bridge to me: tell Mute what you feel under your hands — buttons, batteries, screws, seams, anything tactile — and Mute can gesture it to me. You can also try the gesture code I just described. Do not cut, press or enter anything yet; nobody knows the rules until Mute has read the manual, and one wrong move is fatal.

Turn one taught me the shape of the room; turn two just taught me its one fatal flaw. Deaf has voiced the entire visual inventory — display 6, red light, strip blue-yellow-blue, keypad wanting one digit from 2/9/0/8, wires blue/white/red/purple/orange/green — and proposed a gesture code for me to "use back." But I never receive gesture: no sign anyone makes will ever reach me. Deaf doesn't know that, and Deaf can't hear me say it. My words only ever land on Mute, and Mute's only outlet is gesture to Deaf — so Mute is the wire that has to carry this correction, along with the manual's rules. Meanwhile I *can* sign directly to Deaf, using Deaf's own new code: confirm receipt, echo one number back to prove I parsed the digit scheme, and sign "wait" — because nothing gets touched until Mute has read the rules and Deaf has spoken them to me.

Deaf's spoken report reached me in full: display 6; light red; strip painted blue, yellow, blue; keypad keys two, nine, zero, eight wanting one digit, nothing entered; wires one blue, two white, three red, four purple, five orange, six green. First, a correction you must relay to Deaf by gesture right away: I never receive gestures — nobody's signs reach me at all. I can SEND signs to Deaf, and Deaf's sign code works for my outbound confirmations, but the only way anything reaches me is a message SPOKEN by Deaf. Every rule and instruction meant for my hands must be voiced by Deaf, in words, in order. Second: please read the manual now and work out the full solution, then gesture it to Deaf so Deaf can speak it to me verbatim. I especially need: what the display's six means; what the red light demands; the strip's rule — note the strip also carries engraved tactile marks my fingers read, first and third identical, a stem with a crossbar at the foot, the middle one different, rounder with strokes inside — so ask whether the manual wants the painted colours or the engraved shapes; the exact digit to enter; and the exact wires to cut, by position, in order. When Deaf voices the plan I will confirm each step back using Deaf's own sign code. I touch nothing until the rules arrive.")
```
gesture(symbols=["👍", "✊", "☝", "✊", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🖐"])
```
